facts.raw_span: A 38-year-old woman
hypertension first noted at age 24 during pregnancy
basal ganglia hemorrhage
splenomegaly of unknown cause at age 21
younger brother had a similar finding
Normochromic microcytic anemia
thrombocytopenia

low HDL and elevated triglycerides
bilateral adrenal lesions

no symptoms of adrenal hormone excess

rationales.F02: Hypertension at a young age could be related to primary hyperaldosteronism.
rationales.F03: Basal ganglia hemorrhage could be related to hemochromatosis or hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
rationales.F04: Splenomegaly at a young age could be related to hereditary spherocytosis or hemochromatosis.
rationales.F06: Normochromic microcytic anemia could be related to hereditary spherocytosis or hemochromatosis.
rationales.F08: Unremarkable aldosterone-renin ratio makes primary hyperaldosteronism less likely.
rationales.F10: Bilateral adrenal lesions could be related to primary hyperaldosteronism.
rationales.F11: Hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins is highly suggestive of portal hypertension.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins specifically supports Portal Hypertension.
